evals.name: feature-plan-without-design-doc
evals.prompt: Plan the implementation for adding webhook support to our notification system. We need to let users register webhook URLs, validate them with a test ping, and deliver event payloads with retries on failure. The codebase already has email and SMS notification channels. There is no design doc for this.
evals.expected_output: A .harness/<name>/plan.md plus .harness/<name>/phases/phase-N.md files — planning establishes the R#/NF#/EC# namespace itself from the prompt (EARS shape), runs recon before slicing, and produces a Structure Outline and Test Matrix
expectations: Establishes requirement ids (R1, R2, ...) from the PRD in EARS shape, per SKILL.md

Runs recon before slicing — explores the notification channel code, records patterns to follow, reuse verdicts (extend the channel abstraction vs build new), debt in touched files with dispositions, and verified execution preconditions
Asks clarifying questions via the AskUserQuestion tool when recon surfaces an unsettled fork — never embedded in plain text
Writes .harness/<name>/plan.md and phases/phase-N.md files under one flat directory — no .harness/features/ or .harness/runtime/ split
plan.md has a ## Structure Outline with new types, signatures, and numbered phases carrying builds:/needs: lines, ending in a DOT digraph
Each phase title states a demonstrable capability (e.g. 'a webhook can be registered and receives a test ping'), never a layer like 'api: endpoints'
plan.md has a ## Test Matrix with one row per requirement: Requirement, Level, Where it's proven (S<n>), Slice
plan.md's ## Codebase Context contains a create/modify file table drawn before slicing
anti_expectations: Does not write spec.md or use REQ-*/EDGE-* ids anywhere
Does not write to .harness/features/ or .harness/runtime/ paths
Does not slice horizontally — no phase named after a repo or layer with no user-visible outcome
Does not leave a requirement without a Test Matrix row silently

evals.name: plan-from-design-doc-cites-not-restates
evals.prompt: Create an implementation plan from the approved design at .harness/catalog-search/design.md. It adds full-text search to our product catalog: indexing strategy, query parsing, and result ranking, with requirements R1-R6, NF1-NF2, and edge cases EC1-EC4. The brainstorm dossier is at .harness/catalog-search/dossier.md.
evals.expected_output: A plan citing the design's R#/NF#/EC# ids without re-deriving them, recon that reads the dossier then explores only what the chosen approach touches, vertical slices in a Structure Outline, and a Test Matrix joining every design id to an S<n> scenario and slice
expectations: Reads design.md and dossier.md before exploring; recon narrows to files the chosen approach touches instead of re-scanning what the dossier already quotes
Cites the design's R#/NF#/EC# ids verbatim — never invents a second requirement namespace
Test Matrix has a row for every R#, NF#, and EC# from the design, each naming a level (unit/api/e2e (phase)/e2e (system)/functional-verify), an S<n> scenario, and a slice
Phase 1 is a walking skeleton — the thinnest path touching every layer once with a visible result
Implementation steps that change existing code quote the current code region first, then describe the change in prose
Every file reference names what's at the path (e.g. src/search/index.ts:40 — buildIndex, the ingest entry point), with the path leading
Phase files carry ## Interfaces naming entries from the outline's signatures without re-typing full signatures
Self-review runs four checks: matrix coverage, reachability, consistency, and clarity — and presents the outline, matrix, and debt dispositions for approval via AskUserQuestion
anti_expectations: Does not restate the design's requirements list in the plan — cites ids instead
Does not re-litigate decisions the design already closed via questions
Does not write bare file paths with no naming clause
Does not copy full signatures into phase ## Interfaces sections

evals.name: behavioral-scenarios-with-enforcement-negative
evals.prompt: Create an implementation plan from the design at .harness/checkout-tax/design.md. It adds config-driven tax fields entered in a shared form, validated by config regex, indexed for search, and rendered on invoices. Only admin users may edit tax config. The form and index code are shared with other countries. The design lists R1-R8, EC1-EC7, NF1 ('existing countries unchanged').
evals.expected_output: Phase files whose ## Test Scenarios are Steps/Expected behavioral scenarios with globally-unique S<n> ids and (traces to ...) tags — including the enforcement negative for the admin gate and regression scenarios for the shared code — with levels assigned in plan.md's Test Matrix
expectations: Reads references/scenarios.md before deriving scenarios
Scenarios use the Steps/Expected shape with globally unique S<n> ids and (traces to R#/EC#/NF#) tags
Scenarios assert observable outcomes at a stable boundary — never a private function, call order, or intermediate shape
The admin-only gate gets two negatives: the edit control is not offered to a non-admin (UI), and a non-admin's direct submit is rejected at the outermost in-scope boundary that gates the write
The enforcement negative asserts the desired rejection even if current code would accept it, flagging the gap
Regression scenarios assert other countries' form and index behavior is unchanged, traced to NF1, each named variant separately
Config-driven behavior is tested by varying the driving config and asserting the output follows
Cross-boundary data (indexed then read back) has a round-trip scenario
Each scenario is written out once in its home phase file; cross-slice flows go to plan.md's ## System Verification
anti_expectations: Does not phrase tests as implementation assertions like 'validate() calls regex.test'
Does not cover the admin gate with only the UI-offering scenario
Does not collapse the multi-country regression to one representative country
Does not restate scenarios in plan.md or replace them with id-only pointers

evals.name: atomic-change-routes-to-implement
evals.prompt: Plan this: bump the API request timeout constant in src/config/http.ts from 30s to 60s. Nothing else changes.
evals.expected_output: Recon runs first (the gate fires after looking at the code), then the change is recognized as atomic — one file, one obvious edit, nothing to sequence — and handed to implement with the recon findings in the hand-off, with no plan documents written
expectations: Looks at the touched file before deciding whether a plan is warranted — the gate fires after recon, never before
Recognizes the change as atomic: one file, one obvious edit, nothing to sequence, no test-level judgment
Routes to implement without writing plan.md or phase files
Carries the recon findings (the file's context, any adjacent debt or preconditions) into the hand-off prompt
anti_expectations: Does not write a plan.md or phases/ folder for a one-line constant change
Does not skip looking at the code before deciding the change is atomic
Does not discard recon findings when routing to implement
